paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the Pass@1 rate as a function of the number of reasoning steps. The x-axis, labeled “Num. of Reasoning Steps,” displays a linear scale ranging from 5 to 40, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Pass@1 Rate (%)”, also displays a linear scale from 0 to 100, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 10. A purple line, marked with circular markers, represents the Pass@1 rate for GPT-4o, beginning at approximately 6.5% at the starting value of 5 reasoning steps and increasing to approximately 89.2% at the ending value of 40 reasoning steps. A blue line, marked with diamond markers, represents the Pass@1 rate for Claude-3.5-Sonnet, commencing at approximately 19.4% at 5 reasoning steps and rising to approximately 89.2% at 40 reasoning steps.
